chunks.heading: Cost Optimization
chunks.text:
# Cost Optimization
Model routing: small/fast models for exploration, strong reasoning models for synthesis. Tracking tokens and cost per 100 queries via src/cost.ts.

chunks.heading: Context Window Management
chunks.text:
# Context Window Management
Avoid context bloat. Use sliding window, context compaction, and grounded retrieval of 200-500 token chunks instead of full documents.

chunks.heading: Evaluation Metrics
chunks.text:
# Evaluation Metrics
RAG evaluation: Correctness (percentage of golden queries answered), Groundedness (derived from context), Citation Coverage (must_cite IDs), Refusal Precision.

chunks.heading: Prompt Injection Defenses
chunks.text:
# Prompt Injection Defenses
Direct overrides vs indirect injection in documents. Defenses: strict JSON schemas, XML boundary tags, read-only permissions, verifier gate.

chunks.heading: Agent Execution Loops
chunks.text:
# Agent Execution Loops
ReAct cycle: Observation -> Reasoning -> Action (tool call) -> Observation feedback. Loops until final response or maxIterations.

chunks.heading: Read-Only vs Read-Write Subagents
chunks.text:
# Read-Only vs Read-Write Subagents
Subagents isolate cognitive context. Read-only subagents (spec-auditor, explorer) have Read/Grep tools. Read-write must remain single-threaded.

chunks.heading: MCP Architecture & Roles
chunks.text:
# MCP Architecture & Roles
Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how AI applications interact with data and tools.
Architecture: MCP Host (Claude Code/Cursor), MCP Client, MCP Server.
Communication: Peer-to-peer over JSON-RPC 2.0 messages.

chunks.heading: MCP Error Handling
chunks.text:
# MCP Error Handling
Standard JSON-RPC 2.0 codes: Parse Error (-32700), Invalid Request (-32600), Method Not Found (-32601), Invalid Params (-32602), Internal Error (-32603).
Application errors inside tools return isError: true.

chunks.heading: MCP Prompts
chunks.text:
# MCP Prompts
Reusable server-managed prompt templates discovered via prompts/list and fetched via prompts/get with arguments.
Returns structured messages with dynamic context.

chunks.heading: MCP Lifecycle
chunks.text:
# MCP Lifecycle
1. Initialization: client sends initialize (protocolVersion, capabilities), server responds with serverInfo and capabilities.
2. Initialized: client confirms with notifications/initialized.
3. Normal operation & ping: bidirectional requests and periodic ping messages.

chunks.heading: MCP Resources
chunks.text:
# MCP Resources
Read-only data endpoints exposed via URIs (e.g. file:///path).
Supports dynamic URI templates (RFC 6570) and subscriptions. Client reads via resources/read. Resources have no external side-effects.

chunks.heading: MCP Roots
chunks.text:
# MCP Roots
Defines directory boundaries of filesystem exposed to MCP server via roots/list and notifications/roots/list_changed.
Compliant servers must refuse paths outside roots.

chunks.heading: MCP Sampling
chunks.text:
# MCP Sampling
Allows MCP server to request LLM completions back from host client (sampling/createMessage).
Enables LLM inversion without server needing API keys.

chunks.heading: MCP Security
chunks.text:
# MCP Security
Least privilege principle. Destructive tools require human-in-the-loop approval. Sandboxing, sanitization of inputs against traversal (../), secret scrubbing.

chunks.heading: MCP Tools
chunks.text:
# MCP Tools
Executable actions exposed to LLMs. Declared with name, description, and inputSchema (JSON Schema).
Executed via tools/call with arguments. Returns content and isError boolean. Tools may perform side-effects.

chunks.heading: MCP Transports
chunks.text:
# MCP Transports
Supported transports:
1. stdio: Child process communication via newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout. Stderr is reserved strictly for logging.
2. SSE over HTTP: For remote servers via Server-Sent Events GET text/event-stream and POST.
